findings.title: A bare `status: null` frame settles a running compaction as "stopped"
findings.body: The settle branch fires for `status === null && permissionMode === undefined` even when `compact_result` is absent. In that case a running compaction becomes `interrupted` ("Context compaction stopped") and `context.compaction` is set to null (line 7172). If the CLI or SDK version in use ever sends a plain `status: null` when compaction ends, without `compact_result`, the user sees a spurious "stopped" row. The later `compact_boundary` then finds `context.compaction === null` and adds a second, separate "Context compacted" row. Does every supported Claude CLI version put `compact_result` on the end-of-compaction status frame? The tests only cover frames that carry it, or that carry `permissionMode`.

contracts.action: Claude adapter emits a running compaction item on `status: "compacting"`, settles it on `compact_result` or `status: null`, and completes the same item (same id and ordinal) at `compact_boundary`
contracts.equivalent_path: The `compact_boundary` handler, which before this change emitted a single completed compaction item. The Codex adapter creates its running item from item/started.
contracts.before_after: Before, the item appeared only at the boundary, already completed, so auto-compaction showed no live state. Now a running item is emitted first and reused by the boundary, which adds token counts and keeps `completedAt` from the earlier success frame. A failed or unknown outcome clears `context.compaction`, so a retry creates a new item. Duplicate `compacting` frames while one is running are ignored.
contracts.visible_effect: The web timeline and mobile activity row show "Compacting context", then "Context compacted X → Y tokens", "Context compaction failed" or "Context compaction stopped". Web and mobile `isCompacting` is true while the item is running, so mobile queues follow-ups instead of steering.
contracts.failure_mode: If the turn ends before an outcome frame, `finalizeActiveTurn` (ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:6055-6071) settles the running item as failed, interrupted or cancelled before the terminal event, so no row stays running. If the server dies mid-compaction, the persisted item stays `running`, but clients gate on the active run id and the `inProgress` lifecycle. A bare `status: null` without `compact_result` is treated as an interruption (see finding).

contracts.action: Web and mobile treat failed, interrupted and cancelled compaction items as settled, and treat a running compaction in the active run as compacting
contracts.before_after: Before, only `completed` settled a compaction, so a failed `/compact` kept `isCompacting` true until the run settled. Now every terminal status settles it, and a running item sets `isCompacting` without needing a `/compact` user message. Web and mobile are updated the same way. Web compares the item's run to `activeRuntime.activeRunId` for running and to `activeActivityRun.runId` for settled, a minor inconsistency.
contracts.visible_effect: The compacting spinner and steering lock appear for automatic compaction and clear when it fails or is stopped.
contracts.failure_mode: None found; web gates on busy or running phase and mobile gates on `threadRuntimeIsActive`.

summary: The change emits a running compaction item when Claude reports `status: "compacting"`, settles it on the outcome frame or at turn end, and has the later `compact_boundary` complete the same item. Clients follow in web, mobile and the shared label helper. I read all six files and the unchanged code they depend on, and found no defect I could establish. I could not read the Claude SDK types, so one question is open. It asks whether a plain `status: null` frame, with no `compact_result`, can mark a successful compaction as \"stopped\" and add a second row at the boundary. The new tests cover success, failure, a duplicate `compacting` frame, retry, and the three turn-end paths (result, interrupt, query exit), and they assert event order and item identity.
